scope: Theorem 21.3 (Electric rest-frame extension to finitely many ends) of the manuscript “Spacetime Penrose inequalities: enclosing area, charge, and rigidity” (preprints/Spacetime-Penrose-inequalities-enclosing-area-charge-and-rigidity-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 794bf524061c4b36), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 117. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let (Ω3, g, K, E) be smooth, connected and orientable, complete with its compact smooth boundary S included, and have the finitely many asymptotically flat ends just described. Assume (21.1) everywhere, integrable µ, |J|g, and H + trS K ≤ 0 with the normal into Ω on every component of S. Assume the end falloff of Corollary 21.1 on each end, with a common q > 1/2, and finite ADM limits at the designated end. There is no magnetic field. Let Q0 = 1 4π Z S0 R ⟨E, νR⟩g dAg be its conserved outward charge. Suppose its ADM momentum is zero and that 0 < a0 and r0 ≥ |Q0|, with a0 as in (21.3). Then its ADM energy m0 is positive and (21.4) m0 ≥ 1 2 r0 + Q2 0 r0 ! . No momentum condition is imposed at the other ends.
